correctness.rationale: For squarefree binary sextics, Shaska–Völklein classical criterion identifies the bielliptic divisor as the union of the fifteen matching-determinant hypersurfaces; the ordered-root-to-coefficient map is étale since the Vandermonde is nonzero. At (2,−2,1/2,−1/2,1,−1), independently enumerated all fifteen exact determinants and found precisely two zero factors, (12)(34)(56) and (14)(23)(56), with a nonzero 9/8 two-by-two gradient minor by independent symbolic differentiation. Thus both local branch factors are smooth and transverse and the other thirteen are units. The irreducible family {±1,±a,±a^-1} has both involution matchings, and absence of extra branches and nonzero minor are Zariski-open, so the witness proves a dense-open ordinary crossing. This does not assert the same local singularity in the quotient moduli space.
